Thanks Samir — good ask. Attached is a short readout and the raw sim artifacts: starlight_map_cost_readout_v1.xlsx and batching_simulation_v1.csv. Below is the executive summary and the conservative/optimistic bands you requested.

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline model: open-llm-5b (float16 serving) — baseline tokens-per-dollar: ~33,333 tokens / $1 (approx $0.03 per 1k tokens). This is the reference price we used for the MAP draft.
- Effective tokens/$ with pilot optimizations: 55k (conservative) — 95k (optimistic) tokens per $1. Primary drivers: prefix (KV) caching and request-level batching.
- Key single-number for procurement: we recommend pricing guardrails that assume 55k tokens/$ (conservative) for MAP gating; anything above that is upside.

Assumptions and rationale:
- Traffic profile: 10k DAU, average 2.5 calls per user / day, avg response size 1,200 tokens -> baseline token demand ~30M tokens/day.
- KV/prefix cache: we used a 40% hit rate conservative estimate for session-level repeated prompts (same patient triage flows). With a 40% hit, effective token consumption drops proportionally for cached prefix tokens; net day tokens drop to ~18M. If your frontend implements explicit prefix caching we see up to 55% hit in optimistic scenarios.
- Batching: continuous batching with a 20ms target batch window yields ~1.7x throughput improvement (effective tokens/$ up to ~1.7x) while keeping median tail latency increase <10ms. Longer windows (50–100ms) give 2.1–2.3x improvement but add noticeable tail latency risk for patient-facing flows.
- Quantization: int8 path tested reduces per-token GPU time by ~12–18% with <1% accuracy delta on our eval prompts. Use int8 for non-diagnostic prompts; keep float16 for critical QA flows.

Conservative vs optimistic buckets (tokens per $1):
- Conservative: 33,333 (no optimizations) -> 55,000 (40% cache + moderate batching)
- Optimistic: 33,333 -> 95,000 (55% cache + aggressive batching + int8 on batched inference)

Operational notes / risks:
- Cache invalidation: if you plan to rotate prompt templates or session keys frequently, cache hit will drop; plan a small QA run post-deploy to re-measure.
- Tail latency sensitivity: patient triage requires sub-600ms P95; if MAP requires stricter SLOs we recommend the conservative tokens/$ for procurement.

Attachments: full workbook shows per-route breakdown, sensitivity tables, and per-hour cost projections for pilot traffic. I also attached a small sample payload set (sample_payloads.json) we used for the sim.

Next steps / requested confirmations:
1) Please confirm the traffic distribution in the attached workbook (page: "TrafficProfile") — if avg tokens or calls per DAU are higher, we’ll recompute.
2) Confirm whether you can enable prefix caching in the client before pilot start (expected lift depends on this).
3) Quick sync w/ procurement & infra (30 min) this week to align MAP guardrails.

I'll loop Karthik for kernel/serving specifics once you confirm the traffic profile.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Adding the kernel-level validation and a short checklist. I re-ran the sim with a conservative P90 payload (P50=900 tokens, P90=2,400 tokens) and updated numbers in the workbook (starlight_map_cost_readout_v1.xlsx, tab: "HW-Sims"). Key points: 

- Hardware baseline: A100-like dense kernel (hosted pool); quantized int8 path uses slightly different kernel that reduces per-token GPU time by 14% in our run.
- Effective tokens/$ (conservative P90): ~52k tokens/$1 (this factors in 40% cache hit at P90 distribution + batching window 20ms).
- Effective tokens/$ (optimistic): ~88k tokens/$1 (55% cache, 40ms window, int8 on batched calls).
- Latency trade: P95 with 20ms batch window stays within 520–580ms depending on payload; 40ms window pushes P95 ~630–700ms in worst-case spikes.

Checklist for MAP gating (technical):
1) Confirm P50/P90 payloads in workbook — Ben to get from Starlight.
2) Client-side prefix caching implemented and toggled on in pilot.
3) Agree on batch window cap in MAP (we recommend 20–30ms for patient-facing flows).
4) Decide which routes use int8 vs float16 (we recommend int8 for non-diagnostic summarization routes).
5) Tag routes in the MAP workbook for per-route SLOs so billing projections are route-aware.

If Starlight confirms the P50/P90 numbers, we can update the workbook and produce a single-page MAP appendix that procurement can use for the PO (we'll include conservative tokens/$ guardrail as the default). Proposed short sync: Fri 07/06 09:00 PT (30min).

—Karthik
